Any advice for an introvert working a booth at a conference?

The only thing I can suggest is to try and keep yourself in the moment as much as possible and try to push your social anxiety to the side. If your working a booth it probably means you have material that you can talk about so this is a good starting point.. try to focus on that.

I find that I can be outward for short periods before needing to recharge so it's just a matter of trying to keep that momentum going long enough to get through your conference.

Good luck!!
Thanks for the advice. Stay in the moment, stay in the moment.

I've done a few front-ends of booth in conventions and trade shows and such.

Itll be difficult if you arent used to it but being friendly and receptive as possible to visitors is the best way to get people to your booth. Be attentive of everyone passing by - avoid looking st your phone or getting too engrossed in something to the side. If you see someone take an interest in your booth, don't be afraid to engage them a little and ask them about why they are interested - people LOVE talking about themselves and it takes some pressure off you.

u/slyguy42o also brings up a good point of using your material - come up with a little 2 minute "default" shpeil that covers all the basic information and modify it as the day goes on depending on what gets people interested. If you have a "script" that doesn't sound like it's pre-written you can use it all day and nobody will notice you've been repeating yourself the past 6 hours.

I guess it also depends on the nature of the conference or convention. If there are kids around, engaging them can get the parents interested as well.

It's rough to be around all those people if you're not good with public speaking but the best way is just fake it til you make it. If you feel like you look stupid being friendly or too animated - don't worry because that means you're probably doing it right.
